result.summary: Prevents transactions rejected with result TX_CONSENSUS from being added to the P2P extrapool. The extrapool caches transactions missing from the mempool to assist in compact block reconstruction, but consensus-invalid transactions cannot be part of a valid block.
result.problem: The node adds transactions rejected for consensus invalidity into the extrapool. These transactions waste space in the extrapool cache and cannot help reconstruct valid blocks.
evidence: PR description: 'The extrapool is only used to help reconstruct compact blocks with transactions that for some reason do not fit in our mempool, including consensus invalid transactions... as they are not useful to reconstruct consensus valid blocks.'
result.scope_notes: Very small diff (+3/-2 across 2 files), though the diff was omitted from the prompt.
result.card: Prevents transactions failing validation with TX_CONSENSUS from being added to the P2P extrapool. The extrapool caches transactions that are not in the mempool to assist compact block reconstruction, but consensus-invalid transactions can never appear in a valid block. Caching them consumes pool capacity without providing utility. The author notes this only filters transactions detected as TX_CONSENSUS without adding extra validation overhead for transactions failing under other error categories.

risk.why: If a valid transaction were improperly categorized as TX_CONSENSUS and excluded, compact block reconstruction would fall back to requesting the transaction from peers via an extra round-trip.
